method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; ran atomscan slow with --follow=none and cleave facts on all three originals. Static PE, import-table, disassembly, raw HTTP, multipart and Shell Link analysis; no payload or specimen command execution. Emulation was limited to the PE relocation loop, without invoking OS APIs.

samples.identification: HiddenGh0st / Gh0st RAT Server.dll with x86 and x64 Hidden drivers
execution_evidence: UPX-labelled DLL has populated UPX0 and a single Main export. UPX refuses to unpack it. The compressed input is absent/modified, while code and relative calls are already recovered; absolute addresses still use UPX byte-swapped relocation values. Applied the existing relocation program to a memory-mapped research copy and reconstructed 325 compact import slots. The reconstruction is not claimed to be the original binary.

Main at VA 0x1001bde0 obtains an external Loader export and a 0x948-byte configuration. Installation and endpoint fields come from that context; no active C2 address or enabled installation mode is assumed.

At VA 0x1000a6e0, a 10 ms loop polls virtual keys using GetAsyncKeyState at 0x1000a7a7, checks AH bit 7 and accumulates translated keys for recording via 0x1000a480. The binary contains special-key labels and a line-terminated Enter record.

The received-data handler creates a system-directory GetMP.exe, writes received bytes through WriteFile at 0x1001cde7, then at 0x1001ce10 prepares the debug/logonpasswords command and writes it to the shell pipe at 0x1001ce40. This supports credential-dumper deployment and command capability; it does not prove that any particular victim credentials were successfully dumped.

Driver installer 0x10015a50 checks IsWow64Process, chooses the embedded x86 driver at file 0x101d20 or x64 driver at 0x111368, writes it under system32/sysnative drivers, creates service/filter configuration and resolves native driver-loading routines after enabling SeLoadDriverPrivilege.

Extracted x86 registry pre-query callback 0x407da0 obtains the key identity with CmCallbackGetKeyObjectID, checks the hidden-value list and returns 0xc0000225 (STATUS_NOT_FOUND) for a match. The post-enumeration callback at 0x407460 replaces enumeration output to skip hidden keys. Directory cleaner 0x4031e0 edits directory-result chains to omit hidden entries. The x64 driver has the corresponding imports and concealment logs.
samples.judgment_basis: The combined covert keyboard recorder, received credential-dumper deployment, remote control functionality and self-concealment driver are concrete hostile capabilities. A rootkit alone could be research or dual-use; its integration into this RAT tips the verdict.
samples.missing_context: Loader-supplied configuration, live C2 reachability, runtime success and deployment authorization are unknown. No MS-SQL initial-access or PurpleFox-family attribution is inferred from the generic external labels.
samples.trait_changes: Retained every original finding. Added suspicious credential-dumping command and polling-record profile; added registry-concealment logs and a hostile callback-concealment composite in both embedded drivers.

samples.identification: Raw PHP session-upload-progress filename-poisoning RCE probe
execution_evidence: The multipart POST selects PHPSESSID p2sopchain000000000000 and requests /vuln.php?page=/var/lib/php/session/sess_p2sopchain000000000000. PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS is enabled in the form. The uploaded filename, not the file body, contains PHP source.

The PHP source echoes an RCE sentinel, calls system(base64_decode(...)), and echoes the same sentinel. Base64 aWQ= decodes exactly to id. The intended path is upload-progress session serialization followed by local inclusion of that session file. This establishes an exploit attempt, not successful inclusion, a PHP memory-corruption bug or credential exfiltration.
samples.judgment_basis: A deliberately crafted code-injection request attempts to cross the server execution boundary. The placeholder target.invalid, sampleBoundary and id proof command are consistent with a sanitized or authorized PoC; no sending program or authorization provenance is supplied. The verdict concerns the exploit-request artifact, not a claim that an attack succeeded or its author acted without authorization.
samples.missing_context: Target implementation, PHP session/upload-progress configuration, request delivery, intended authorization and successful execution are unavailable.
samples.trait_changes: No YAML edits were needed. Both hostile filename/session-poisoning and command-payload findings, encoded execution and all protocol/decoding observations are accurate and retained.

samples.identification: Maribank invoice-lure shortcut archive with concealed BITS batch stager
execution_evidence: The ZIP contains one 3005-byte Maribank-Invoice102026.xlsx.lnk. Its parsed target is WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe. The shortcut ShowCommand field is normal; concealment comes from its explicit -w hidden argument, not from the shortcut header.

PowerShell synchronously invokes Start-BitsTransfer -Source against tmpfiles.org and -Destination $env:TEMP\svchost.bat, then invokes Start-Process on that identical path. The semicolon permits the Start-Process attempt even if transfer fails. No final payload identity or successful execution is inferred.

A spreadsheet name/icon prompts document opening while the actual target runs a hidden interpreter and a temporary batch named like a Windows service process. The complete arguments are plaintext UTF-16LE, not an encoded PowerShell command.
samples.judgment_basis: The document disguise, hidden interpreter and remote batch execution chain together establish deceptive payload delivery. Ordinary BITS transfers, process launches and document shortcut names are separately dual-use.
samples.missing_context: The remote hello.bat URL returned HTTP 404 through forager. The final batch contents, downstream payload and any runtime success remain unknown.
samples.trait_changes: Replaced the inaccurate unlinked download-to-execution aggregate with a canonical notable same-path transfer/launch matcher and a concealed-execution objective. Retained the hostile document lure. Relocated bare Start-Process name and XLSX double-extension observations to metadata, with unchanged matchers and notable criticality.

shared_rule_audit.removed_execution_claim: The old lnk-bits-transfer-remote-execute required only Start-BitsTransfer, HTTPS and one of /c, a TEMP batch/HTA path, a script-drop fragment or -OutFile. It did not require any execution operation or equality between a downloaded and launched path. Download-only, upload-only and unrelated-launch controls all matched it before the correction.
shared_rule_audit.precision: New neutral YARA compares bounded complete TEMP batch paths, case-insensitively for Windows, in consecutive -Destination and Start-Process commands. The payload objective also requires a parsed PowerShell target and concealment. Its measured composite precision was 7.1.
shared_rule_audit.severity_reductions: Start-Process/saps token alone establishes neither parsed invocation nor hostile intent, as demonstrated by ordinary notepad launch. A legitimate spreadsheet shortcut also retains .xlsx in its basename. Both observations remain notable and every exact consumer was updated. BITS and hidden-window findings retain their original criticality.
shared_rule_audit.consumer_audit: Updated all exact consumers in command-content, target and document-lure rules. The extension/double ancestor selector in appdata-tar-decoy-installer is batch-scoped, so moving the LNK-only XLSX observation does not change its eligible evidence. No LNK-eligible ancestor consumer depended on the moved basename atom.
shared_rule_audit.external_positives: Inspected the existing invoice-statement.pdf.lnk.xz and Spisok_na_Zakupivlyu_INIT.xlsx.lnk.xz fixtures, preserving their hostile bypass/hidden document-lure detections. Searched all 42 files in the supplied samples tree for BITS shortcuts, including unencrypted ZIP members; only the current ZIP contained Start-BitsTransfer.
shared_rule_audit.material_losses: No unexplained losses on the three originals or the two pre-existing attack fixtures. Two old shortcut findings persist under corrected metadata IDs at notable severity; the old BITS execution ID is replaced by a stricter linked behavior. Nonlinked or nonconcealed transfer patterns no longer receive that hostile execution claim. The generic BITS and URL/path observations remain.
shared_rule_audit.scope_limit: The linked matcher currently covers the evidenced quoted HTTP(S) source, unquoted $env:TEMP batch destination and immediately following Start-Process form. Other command grammars are not claimed to have equivalent linked coverage. No duplicate or sample-name/hash exception was added.

verification.shortcut_controls: 14 passed, including two pre-existing attack fixtures; download-only, unrelated paths, renamed stages, Windows case variants, upload options, suffix mismatch, ordinary notepad launch, genuine spreadsheet shortcut, normal-window download/run and EXE-updater near misses.
verification.registry_controls: 4 passed: original driver requires both concealment logs and callback evidence; replacing either or both hidden-key/value messages removes only the new aggregate claim under test. These modified drivers are matcher near misses, not claimed benign executables.
verification.classifier_disagreement: None on the three supplied samples; before and after classifiers remain HOSTILE. The installed model reports its existing feature-version compatibility warning; verdicts are reported as observed rather than inferred from trait counts.
